project: Engine Character and String System Planning
goal: Introduce one engine-owned character and string layer that keeps internal/editor text UTF-8-first, describes platform-native character types explicitly, provides allocator-aware owning strings and non-owning string views, and rejects implicit auto-transcoding that would obscure ImGui and platform API boundaries.

checkpoints.title: Define explicit character taxonomy and literal policy
must_be_true_after: Engine text code no longer treats plain `char` as the implicit answer for all platform or wide-character paths.
A single core header defines `Char8`, `Char16`, `Char32`, `WideChar`, `PlatformChar`, and narrow/UTF aliases with compile-time platform selection.

Static text literals follow explicit character domains: UTF-8 literals stay narrow by default, while platform-native literals use an explicit engine macro or literal helper instead of silent reinterpretation.
Platform-native text is named separately from UTF text so Windows wide APIs, ImGui narrow APIs, and non-Windows UTF-8 paths are not mixed accidentally.

checkpoints.title: Introduce allocator-aware engine string aliases
must_be_true_after: The first implementation uses `std::basic_string` with `MoerStlAllocator` instead of creating a fake wrapper around the STL container.

`BasicString<CharT, Traits, Allocator>` and `BasicStringView<CharT, Traits>` exist in the engine namespace with concrete aliases for `String`, `StringView`, `WideString`, `WideStringView`, `PlatformString`, and `PlatformStringView`.
Owning strings default to the engine allocator; views remain allocator-free and non-owning.
The public API exposes direct STL-compatible behavior through aliases, not pass-through member functions or adapter classes.

checkpoints.title: Make compile-time strings and static literals encoding-aware
must_be_true_after: `CompileTimeString` remains a small compile-time storage utility but is moved or included through the new string boundary.
Compile-time string deduction works for supported character storage types without hard-coding narrow `char` behavior.
Static literals that must follow `PlatformChar` use one explicit macro or literal entry point at the call site; the engine does not guess and auto-convert unrelated string literals.
The utility does not perform transcoding; it only preserves literal character type and size.

checkpoints.title: Add explicit conversion and third-party boundary rules
must_be_true_after: No implicit conversion exists between UTF, wide, and platform strings.
Any required conversion API is named by source and destination encoding, for example UTF-8 to platform and platform to UTF-8.
ImGui-facing UI text stays UTF-8 narrow and is passed to ImGui as narrow literals, `const char*`, or UTF-8 string/view storage without hidden transcoding or temporary conversion buffers.
Unsupported or invalid input policy is explicit before implementation: reject invalid sequences or replace them, but never silently reinterpret bytes as characters.

checkpoints.title: Migrate core aliases without compatibility shims
must_be_true_after: `misc/STL.h` includes the new string header and exposes engine string aliases from one canonical location.
New runtime/editor code uses engine string names when ownership or platform text semantics matter.
ImGui call sites remain on the UTF-8 narrow path; only platform API boundaries and explicitly wide text paths use `PlatformString` or `WideString`.
No parallel legacy typedefs, deprecated aliases, implicit conversion wrappers, or compatibility shims are kept after migration.

checkpoints.title: Validate with existing repository scripts only
must_be_true_after: Header-only alias changes compile through the existing core/editor build instead of a new standalone test harness.
If conversion code is added, it is covered through existing test targets or existing repository test scripts, not an ad-hoc script.
Validation starts with `just b` when available; otherwise use the repository CMake build path already documented for the project.
On Linux, use existing `testscripts/linux/test_taskgraph.sh` only when the touched code affects that tested area; on Windows, use `testscripts/windows/test_all.ps1` for the broader existing suite.

design_notes.canonical_headers: Use `source/runtime/core/include/string/CharTypes.h` for character storage aliases and `source/runtime/core/include/string/String.h` for owning/view string aliases. Keep `misc/STL.h` as an aggregate include only.
design_notes.preferred_first_version: Use aliases over `std::basic_string` and `std::basic_string_view` with `MoerStlAllocator`. Do not implement a custom string container until the engine has a concrete invariant that STL cannot express.
design_notes.platform_character_rule: `PlatformChar` is `wchar_t` on Windows and UTF-8 storage on non-Windows targets. Treat it as platform API boundary text, not as the engine's universal internal encoding.
design_notes.internal_encoding_rule: Prefer UTF-8 engine `String` for persisted data, logs, configs, asset paths after normalization, editor text, and ImGui-facing text unless a platform API requires `PlatformString`.
design_notes.conversion_rule: Conversions must be explicit and named. Do not add constructors or overloads that silently convert between `String`, `WideString`, and `PlatformString`.
design_notes.allocator_rule: Owning engine strings use `MoerStlAllocator` by default. `StringView` aliases never own memory and must not outlive the storage they reference.
design_notes.rejection_rule: Do not add a wrapper class that only forwards STL methods. Add a real class only when it owns a stable invariant such as small-buffer policy, normalized encoding, or allocator state that aliases cannot enforce.
design_notes.preferred_char_policy: Prefer explicit character-domain ownership. Users write UTF-8 text normally for engine/editor/ImGui code and opt into `PlatformChar` through one explicit macro or helper only when a platform-native literal is actually required.
design_notes.static_literal_rule: Do not wrap every string literal in the codebase. Keep ordinary engine and ImGui literals narrow UTF-8. Reserve the engine text macro/literal helper for platform-native or explicitly non-UTF-8 literal domains.
design_notes.imgui_rule: Treat ImGui as a hard narrow-text boundary. Its labels, IDs, format strings, and input buffers stay on UTF-8 `char` storage. Do not insert an automatic conversion layer in front of ImGui APIs.
design_notes.no_auto_transcode_rule: Do not add wrappers that auto-convert string types at call sites. They hide allocation, lifetime, and encoding failure behavior, and they are especially wrong for hot ImGui/UI paths.

validation: Planning only in this checkpoint. No implementation is part of this file.
